The FOMC statement already conveyed a sharp deterioration in activity, jobs, inflation, and impaired credit, offset in part by aggressive policy easing and liquidity support. The April 2020 SLOOS reinforces the impairment in credit flow: banks tightened standards and terms broadly across C&I (including middle‑market firms), CRE and multifamily loans, and HELOCs; widened loan-rate spreads; raised costs of credit lines; and cited COVID-19, weaker economic outlook, and liquidity needs as key drivers. Demand weakened notably in CRE/multifamily, and many banks expected further tightening, though there were pockets of increased inquiries and isolated stronger demand in some mortgage segments and select clients. Taken together, SLOOS evidence of materially tighter bank credit conditions outweighs the policy mitigants, making the overall tone more negative than previously assessed.
